key_insight: Neural networks can end up behaving similarly on the same final task while still preserving distinct internal representations shaped by their earlier training history.
engineering_relevance: For constitutive modeling and other predictive systems, matching output accuracy does not guarantee equivalent internal state, so training protocol can leave persistent hidden biases that matter for interpretability and transfer.
method: Paired CNNs start from identical weights but see reversed task orders before a shared deterministic relaxation phase.
Track behavioral matching, prediction disagreement, and a representation-history score across MNIST and rotated-MNIST controls.
Compare against a ReLU-LeakyReLU control and linear-probe access to class information.
evidence_signal: Across 20 MNIST pairs, 16 met the behavioral-matching criterion, yet matched models still showed a mean history score of 0.139 and about 3.1% prediction disagreement; similar persistence remained after 50,000 updates and in rotated-MNIST controls.
watch_item: The findings are protocol-scoped, so the persistence of history effects may depend on architecture, activation choice, dataset, and the specific training schedule used.
paper_title: Behavioral Convergence Without Representational Convergence: Persistent Training-History Dependence in Neural Networks
